paper.title: MATTERIX: toward a digital twin for robotics-assisted chemistry laboratory automation

assembly: Author Toronto glovebox CAD with two separate native NVIDIA UR3e assets, locally assembled in a reconstructed laboratory.
boundaries: The complete room layout and robot placements are local reconstruction, not recovered paper coordinates.
Four front ports and side transfer chambers/door are structurally consistent with Figure 3; exact source revision equivalence is unverified.
The robots retain bare flanges; exact Figure 3 grippers, black glove sleeves and door/hatch dynamics are missing.
This is a zero-physics static inspection; physical task execution, contact stability and full reproduction remain unverified.
Other stations retain separately documented source approximations.
Only native screenshots and source metadata are included; no CAD/USD files or private local paths are redistributed.
license: No repository CAD redistribution license located in the fixed branch tree; raw source assets excluded.

visible: Four hood assemblies, liquid station, solid station, wash station, mobile model and new Toronto box are visible.
The Toronto box stands on the local bench and contains two distinct physical arm assets.
limitations: Original metric laboratory layout and full apparatus inventory are not recovered.
Empty hood interiors and simplified solid/wash fixtures remain.
This distant view cannot resolve millimeter support gaps or validate task functionality.

visible: Four front glove ports, left transfer chamber, right side door and red handles are clearly visible.
Two physical UR3e bodies are distinguishable; bases appear seated on the actual source floor with no obvious floating.
Both end-effectors remain visibly bare; missing task grippers are not concealed.
limitations: Reflective rear aluminum produces additional blurred arm and room silhouettes; these are reflections, not additional physical robots.
Glass reflection/haze and bright low-contrast CAD reduce detail.
Black glove sleeves and task instruments are absent.
Visual support appearance complements CPU support sampling; it is not settled-contact evidence.

visible: Both physical bases and substantial parts of both arms are visible through unchanged source glass.
Author side door frame, transfer chamber and source floor/bench contact are clearly exposed.
limitations: The right door frame partly occludes the nearer arm.
Rear aluminum reflections create visually duplicated robot silhouettes.
This oblique screenshot cannot establish fully unobstructed two-arm inspection or photometric correspondence to Figure3.

robot_count_note: There are two physical UR3e assets inside the glovebox. The source aluminum rear panels reflect additional robot silhouettes.
